name: 16 Nocna Ściema
description: Nocna Ściema is a unique night road race in Koszalin, offering three distances: 7 km, a half marathon, and a marathon. The course runs through the city streets, with the start and finish at the ZOS “Bałtyk” Stadium. The race has official PZLA certification, ensuring accurate course measurement and the possibility of setting records. The event has a one-of-a-kind atmosphere, with a laser start at 2:00 a.m. highlighting its unique nocturnal character. Participants can expect excellent organization, attractive prizes, and keepsakes.
course_highlights: PZLA-certified course, confirming accurate measurement
A loop of approximately 7 km, completed multiple times depending on the distance
Start and finish at the ZOS “Bałtyk” Stadium in Koszalin
additional: The race starts at 2:00 a.m. with a laser start. The race office for children and young people is located at the Koszalin University of Technology Sports Hall. The course runs through the streets of Koszalin, with views of exhibits at the aviation museum. After each distance, children receive gifts and prizes directly at the stadium. The course is undulating, and runners can rest at the stadium, which the loop passes through.

name: Chwałowicki Maraton Napoleoński
organizer: Stowarzyszenie na rzecz Rozwoju i Integracji Chwałowic
description: The Chwałowice Napoleonic Marathon is a small-scale running event held in the picturesque village of Chwałowice, surrounded by forests and fields. The marathon course runs through wooded and rural areas, offering runners peace and contact with nature, with a distinctive point on the loop at Napoleon’s Stone. The race has a friendly, informal character, without competitive pressure or crowds, creating a welcoming atmosphere for logging miles together. The organizers, including local runner Arek Tołłoczko, take care of course markings and participants’ comfort. In 2024, a series of four marathons on this course is planned, taking place at different times of the year.
course_highlights: A 42.195 km course through forests and picturesque fields
A loop featuring the distinctive Napoleon’s Stone as a landmark
Every kilometre marked, with the start/finish on Polna Street
additional: A 7 km running route laid out and marked by the Harcownik Running Club from Jelcz-Laskowice; convenient parking; no crowds and a relaxed atmosphere without competitive pressure; a planned series of four marathons in 2024, taking place in winter, spring, summer and autumn. Sources describe a 42.195 km marathon course; there is no confirmed information about the entry fee or registration for the 2027 edition.

name: XIV Bieg Nadwiślański Szlakiem Doliny D... (Tczew)
description: The Bieg Nadwiślański Szlakiem Dolnej Doliny Wisły is an annual running event held in Tczew County. The event features two races: a PZLA-certified marathon of 42.195 km and a half marathon of 21.097 km. The routes pass through the scenic Vistula Valley, over a mix of asphalt and gravel surfaces, with traffic restricted during the race. The start and finish are located in Tczew, and the event attracts runners from various regions, offering professional organization and clearly marked routes.
course_highlights: A PZLA-certified 42.195 km marathon through Tczew and nearby towns
A 21.097 km half marathon on an asphalt-and-gravel route
The course is marked with road markings and signs at 1 km intervals; traffic is restricted during the race
additional: The participant limit is 400 paid entrants. The marathon starts at 09:00 at the School Complex of Construction and Clothing in Tczew; the half marathon starts at 11:00 at the Primary School in Małe Walichnowy. The start line closes 15 minutes after the start. The marathon course is PZLA-certified; the half marathon course is not. The course is marked with road markings and signs at 1 km intervals.

name: XLIV Perła Paprocan
description: Perła Paprocan is a marathon held around Lake Paprocany in Tychy on a 7 km loop. Participants can choose any distance by running multiples of the loop, up to a full marathon. The event is recreational and intended for training, with no need to declare a distance in advance. Every participant receives a commemorative medal at the finish. The organizers emphasize that the atmosphere and sense of community among runners matter more than competition. Tychy is the only city in Poland where a marathon is held twice a year, and Perła Paprocan is one of those editions.
course_highlights: A 7 km loop around Lake Paprocany
Paved sections (over 50%), along with compacted paths and forest trails
A station with drinks, fruit, and sweets after each loop
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the Irysy restaurant by Lake Paprocany in Tychy (ul. Parkowa 17) on October 23, 2026, from 14:00 to 17:00; October 24, 2026, from 10:00 to 15:00; and on race day from 8:00 to 9:30. A third party may collect a race number with written authorization. Participants under 18 must have consent from a parent or guardian. Valuables can be left in the storage area, marked with the race number.

description: Gliwicka Parkowa Prowokacja Biegowa is a series of 12 running and Nordic walking events held in Gliwice, in the municipal forest. The events take place once a month on Saturdays, and the 4,219.5 m course runs mainly along forest paths and gravel tracks, with sections of asphalt. The event promotes a healthy, active outdoor lifestyle and encourages regular exercise under the slogan “Let yourself be provoked into fighting laziness!”
course_highlights: A 4,219.5 m course along forest paths, gravel tracks and asphalt
Start and finish in the Municipal Forest near Piast Stadium
A refreshment point with drinks available after each lap
additional: Events take place on Saturdays once a month. The time limit for running and Nordic walking is 3 hours; e-Prowokacja has no time limit. Participants can complete 1 to 5 laps (from about 4.2 km to approximately half-marathon distance). Race bibs are valid for the whole year and must be returned after each race. After the event, participants receive a drink and a snack (sausage or banana), as well as a bar through a prize draw, if sanitary regulations allow. Several starts can be paid for in advance; unused fees carry over to subsequent months. This is a recurring event; information about the date and registration for the edition on 30 October 2027 has not been confirmed in available sources.

The organizers offer training plans tailored to different experience levels to help participants prepare optimally for the race. The event is part of the TreningBiegacza.pl running calendar, which promotes road races and supports runners in their development.

10 km distance in Opole
Opportunity to prepare with dedicated training plans
additional: The organizers offer expert support and detailed training instructions. Participants can use a platform to manage the race listing and collaborate on marketing. Training plans ranging from 8 to 20 weeks are available, tailored to the runner’s VDOT level.

description: Gorlicki Mountain Run is an annual running event held in the picturesque Low Beskids, near Radocyna and Wysowa-Zdrój. The race offers three distances: 8.2 km, 24.4 km, and a Vertical race to Magura Małastowska. The courses feature significant elevation gain and beautiful views, and the participant limit is strictly controlled, ensuring an intimate atmosphere. The organizers provide professional race services, awards ceremonies, and cash prizes. Taking part is an excellent opportunity to test your strength on mountain terrain.
course_highlights: 24.4 km course with 610 m of elevation gain
8.2 km course with 160 m of elevation gain
2.3 km Vertical race with 340 m of elevation gain to Magura Małastowska
additional: Participant limits: 24 km — 250 people, 8 km — 150 people, Vertical — 150 people. The start and finish for the 8 km and 24 km races are at the State Forests Centre in Radocyna; the Vertical race starts at Magura Ski Park / Małastów. Time limits: 5 hours for 24 km, 1 hour for the Vertical. Entry fee refunds are available until 31.10.2027. Race bibs must be visible on the front of shirts or shorts.

Marceliński Bieg Jesienny 2026
description: Marceliński Autumn Run 2026 is a cross-country race organized in Poznań by running enthusiasts from the Biegi.Wlkp. group. The event takes place on scenic courses that showcase the location’s aesthetic appeal. Since 2014, the organizers have focused on promoting cross-country running in Wielkopolska, offering participants a unique running experience in beautiful natural surroundings.
course_highlights: A cross-country race on scenic routes in Poznań
Courses that showcase the location’s aesthetic appeal
Organized by experienced running enthusiasts from Wielkopolska
additional: The race route is available on Garmin Connect. Race packs can be collected using an authorization form template. Cross-country race, event in Marceliński Forest, November 8, 2026, puzzle-piece medals, forest routes

name: 14. PKO Bieg Niepodległości w Rzeszowie
description: The 14th PKO Independence Run in Rzeszów is an annual running event organized by the Rzeszów Running Club “Rzeszów Biega,” in partnership with the Rzeszów City Hall and PKO Bank Polski. The 10 km main race starts and finishes at Rzeszów Market Square and takes place on November 11 at 11:11. The event promotes an active lifestyle and running in the Podkarpackie region, offering age-group classifications and special categories, including for doctors and lawyers. Participants receive a race pack with a T-shirt, bib number and chip, and a commemorative medal at the finish. description: What sets the Nieuchwytni Run apart from other events is its regionally unique “moving finish line” format. Participants do not run toward a designated point; instead, they try to stay ahead of the pursuit team for as long as possible. The runners will start at 10:00, and exactly 15 minutes later the “finish line” will set off along the course—a cyclist and a car equipped with professional timing equipment. The moment these vehicles overtake a runner marks the end of their race, and their result is recorded. The pursuit team will gradually increase its speed, from an initial 15 km/h to 35 km/h in the final stage of the race.

name: II Bieg Transgranicznej Przyjaźni
description:
A 5-kilometre main race, a Nordic walking event over the same distance, and shorter races for children in the Young Athlete Zone. The event opens the Polish-Czech Grand Prix series, which concludes a month later in Ludgeřovice.

Course: moderately easy, with a new route this year

We have changed the route compared with the first edition. Four kilometres now run along Teligi and Czarnieckiego streets—on asphalt, with plenty of space and no tight turns. It’s a stretch where you can keep a steady pace from start to finish.

Only the final kilometre goes through post-mining areas. The surface gets uneven, but it’s just five minutes of running—and also the most interesting part of the course. You run through a part of Silesia that is coming back to life.

The total elevation gain is 18 metres, spread across the whole distance. There are no climbs that disrupt your rhythm. It’s a good course for your first-ever five kilometres, and a fair one for anyone looking to test their time—as long as you save some strength for the finish.
additional:
The event is part of the “Pink October” campaign and promotes breast cancer prevention. It is organised by the “Srebrne Nici” Association, with the Czech club BK Ludgeřovice as its partner.

Photos from the previous edition.

name: XXV Bieg Sobiborski "Ocalić od zapomnienia - uczyć dla przyszłości"
organizer: Miejski Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji we Włodawie
description: The start is at 12:00 by the Sobibór Museum and Memorial to the Victims, on county road No. 1727L along the Żłobek–Sobibór–Wołczyny section. After approximately 300 m, runners cross the tracks of railway line No. 81 Chełm–Włodawa and run to provincial road 816. They then follow provincial road 816 towards Włodawa. After approximately 8.5 km, runners cross the tracks of railway line No. 81 Chełm–Włodawa again and run through the village of Orchówek to Włodawa, continuing along Okunińska Street, Rynek Street and J. Piłsudski Avenue, with the finish at 4 Szkolna Street.
additional:
“There are places in our country marked especially by the blood of thousands of victims murdered in the cruellest way and in the name of the most despicable of ideologies—the ideology of hatred. One such place is Sobibór, where, in just over a dozen months (1942–1943), the Nazis managed to murder approximately a quarter of a million people, especially people of Jewish nationality.”

The race is an unusual history lesson for society. It contributes to achieving sporting goals and also helps instil in the younger generation a remembrance of the tragic history of the extermination camp in Sobibór.

name: Bieg Wolności Podatkowej
description:

On June 13, participants can take on the 5 km or 10 km distance, either in person in Wrocław or virtually from anywhere in Poland. The main event will take place at the Olympic Stadium, and the route follows a scenic loop along the Oder. Flat and scenic—ideal running conditions in the City of a Hundred Bridges.

Every step has extra meaning here. Race participants support the “Na Ratunek Dzieciom z Chorobą Nowotworową” Foundation, showing that the energy of sport can make a real difference to others. It’s a great opportunity to combine physical activity with supporting an important cause.

Participants will also receive a generous race pack prepared by IFIRMA: the official race T-shirt, a finisher’s medal, a race bib, a reusable cup, a sports bag, and a certificate for a tree of their own in the IFIRMA forest in Oleśnica.

Join the 2026 Tax Freedom Run and celebrate freedom actively!
